files.lesson.md: --- order: 14 unit: solving node: AC9M8A02 n3 assumes: [AC9M8A02 n1] # graphing inequalities: Linear relations, Lines and regions; the boards here draw the lines title: Inequalities summary: "Solve an inequality like an equation, doing the same to both sides, but when you multiply or divide by a negative, reverse the inequality sign. Show the answer on a number line: open circle for < and >, closed for ≤ and ≥. Check with a value." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "You need more than 50 points to pass, and a ride needs riders at least 120 cm tall. Not one answer: a whole range of them." connection: load-limit # data/connections/maths.yml (documentation only) app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8177 url: http://127.0.0.1:8177/index.html readySelector: "#legend" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: boards.yml#explain, caption: "$-2x$ is more than 6 (the line above the dashed one) to the left of $x = -3$: the solution of $-2x > 6$ is $x < -3$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@boards.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Dividing by a negative turns it round" say: "Dividing by a negative reverses the inequality." clip: - caption: { text: "−2x > 6. The line y = −2x is above y = 6 on the left of x = −3.", say: "Minus two x is more than six on the left of minus three." } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "So x < −3. Dividing by −2 reversed > into <.", say: "So x is less than minus three. Dividing by minus two turned it round." } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "Check x = −4: −2 × (−4) = 8, and 8 > 6. ✓", say: "Check: minus four gives eight, and eight is more than six." } - wait: 1400 --- An **inequality** compares two sides with $<$, $>$, $\le$ or $\ge$. Its solution is usually a whole range of values, such as $x < 5$, which you can show on a number line. You solve it like an equation, doing the same to both sides, with one new rule. This lesson finds the rule, and why it works. ## Predict: a negative in front ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a solution of −2x > 6 shows whether they divide by −2 and keep the sign, the slip this lesson is built around." check: type: predict q: "Which is the solution of $-2x > 6$?" options: - "$x < -3$" - "$x > -3$" - "$x > 3$" - "$x < 3$" actual: "x < −3. Check x = −4: −2 × (−4) = 8, and 8 > 6. But x = 0 (which x > −3 allows) gives 0, and 0 > 6 is false." ``` Pick a value from your answer and check it in $-2x > 6$. ## Run: when is −2x more than 6? ```step stage: run insight: "Dragging P along y = −2x to where it is above y = 6 shows the solution lies to the left of −3: the sign turned round." try: { playground: board, starter: "boards.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "$P$ is on the line $y = -2x$. Drag it to a point where $-2x$ is more than 6 (above the dashed line). Was your prediction right?", when: "P on y = -2x and y(P) > 6" } ``` Where are all the points that work: left or right of $x = -3$? ## Investigate: solve, show, check ```step stage: investigate insight: "Adding, subtracting, and multiplying or dividing by a positive keep the inequality sign; multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses it, because it flips the order on the number line. Mia keeps the inequality sign after dividing by −2." try: { playground: board, starter: "boards.yml#ray", height: 380 } tasks: - starter: "boards.yml#ray" hint: ["3x − 4 < 11: add 4, then divide by 3.", "x < 5: open circle at 5 (5 itself is not included), shade left."] check: { type: board, text: "Solve $3x - 4 < 11$, then show the solution: move $P$, choose the circle and the direction.", when: "x(P) = 5 and k = 0 and s = -1", explain: "3x < 15, so x < 5: an open circle at 5, shaded left." } - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#mia" text: "Mia solves $-2x > 6$. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: inequality-reverse explain: "Line 3: dividing by −2 reverses the inequality sign, so x < −3. Her check on line 4 fails, which is the clue: x = 0 should work if x > −3 were right." - check: type: question q: "Which is the solution of $-3x \\le 12$?" options: ["$x \\ge -4$", "$x \\le -4$", "$x \\ge 4$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Dividing by −3 reverses ≤ into ≥.", "12 ÷ (−3) is −4, not 4."] explain: "Divide by −3 and reverse: x ≥ −4. Check x = 0: 0 ≤ 12. ✓" ``` ### Solve, show, check Here is how to solve and show an inequality. ```worked 3x - 4 < 11 :: Solve like an equation: do the same to both sides. 3x < 15 :: Add 4 to both sides: the sign stays. x < 5 :: Divide by 3 (positive): the sign stays. \text{open circle at } 5,\ \text{shaded left} :: On a number line: an open circle at 5 ($<$: 5 is not included; $\le$ would be closed), shaded left. -2x > 6 \;\Rightarrow\; x < -3 :: Divide by $-2$ (negative): **reverse** the inequality sign. $2 < 3$ but $-2 > -3$: a negative flips the order. x = -4:\; 8 > 6\; \checkmark :: Check a value from the solution in the first inequality. ``` Now solve $3x - 4 < 11$ and show it on the board. ### Find the mistake Read Mia's working. Her check is a clue. ### Divide by a negative ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a closed circle, a negative x term, a fraction, then a range between two values, and the edge case: why the inequality sign reverses." try: { playground: board, starter: "boards.yml#ray", height: 380 } tasks: - starter: "boards.yml#ray" hint: "2x ≥ 4, so x ≥ 2: a closed circle (2 is included)." check: { type: board, text: "Solve $2x + 3 \\ge 7$ and show it.", when: "x(P) = 2 and k = 1 and s = 1", explain: "2x ≥ 4, x ≥ 2: closed circle at 2, shaded right." } - check: type: question q: "Solve $5 - x > 2$." options: ["$x < 3$", "$x > 3$", "$x > -3$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "−x > −3: dividing by −1 reverses the inequality sign.", "Take 5 from both sides: −x > −3."] explain: "−x > −3, then divide by −1 and reverse: x < 3. Check x = 0: 5 > 2. ✓" - starter: "boards.yml#ray" hint: ["Add 1: x/2 < 4.", "Multiply by 2 (positive): x < 8."] check: { type: board, text: "Solve $\\dfrac{x}{2} - 1 < 3$ and show it.", when: "x(P) = 8 and k = 0 and s = -1", explain: "x/2 < 4, x < 8: open circle at 8, shaded left." } - check: type: answer q: "A range: how many integers $x$ have $-1 < x \\le 4$?" answer: "5" feedback: - ["6", "−1 is not included (<), so start at 0."] - ["4", "4 is included (≤)."] explain: "0, 1, 2, 3, 4: five integers. −1 is left out (open), 4 is in (closed)." - check: type: question q: "Edge case: $2 < 5$. Multiply both sides by $-1$. Which is true?" options: ["$-2 > -5$", "$-2 < -5$", "$-2 = -5$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "On a number line, −2 is to the right of −5, so −2 is more.", "They are not equal."] explain: "Multiplying by −1 reflects every number about 0, so the order flips: 2 < 5 but −2 > −5. That is why the inequality sign reverses." ``` ### A closed circle Each task changes one thing. ### A negative x ### A fraction ### A range ### Why it reverses ## Practise: inequalities ```step stage: practise insight: "Solving with and without reversal, reading a number line and the largest integer, mixed; the review keeps equations fresh." tasks: - check: type: question q: "Solve $4x + 1 \\ge -7$." options: ["$x \\ge -2$", "$x \\le -2$", "$x \\ge 2$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Dividing by 4 (positive) keeps the sign.", "−7 − 1 = −8, and −8 ÷ 4 = −2."] explain: "4x ≥ −8, x ≥ −2." - check: type: question q: "Solve $-5x < 20$." options: ["$x > -4$", "$x < -4$", "$x > 4$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Dividing by −5 reverses the inequality sign.", "20 ÷ (−5) = −4."] explain: "Divide by −5 and reverse: x > −4. Check x = 0: 0 < 20. ✓" - picture: { ref: boards.yml#pic-less-5, caption: "A solution on a number line." } check: type: question q: "Which inequality does this number line show?" options: ["$x < 5$", "$x \\le 5$", "$x > 5$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The circle is open: 5 is not included.", "The ray goes left: smaller values."] explain: "Open circle at 5, shaded left: x < 5." - check: type: answer q: "Review: solve $3x + 2 = 2x + 7$." answer: "5" feedback: - ["9", "Take 2x from both sides: x + 2 = 7."] explain: "x + 2 = 7, x = 5. Check: 17 = 17." ``` ### Positive coefficient ### Negative coefficient ### Read the line ### Review: equations ## Make: write one with a negative ```step stage: make insight: "Writing an inequality with a negative x term whose solution is x ≥ −2, then showing it, reverses the lesson: from the solution back to an inequality that needs the reversal." try: { playground: board, starter: "boards.yml#ray", height: 380 } hint: ["Start from x ≥ −2 and multiply both sides by −3: the sign reverses.", "−3x ≤ 6. Check x = 0: 0 ≤ 6. ✓"] check: { type: board, text: "Write an inequality with $-3x$ in it whose solution is $x \\ge -2$. Solve it on paper, then show the solution on the line.", when: "x(P) = -2 and k = 1 and s = 1", explain: "For example −3x ≤ 6, or 1 − 3x ≤ 7. Dividing by −3 reverses ≤ into ≥: x ≥ −2." } ``` Swap with a partner: solve theirs, and check a value. ## Make: a trailer load, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A load limit is an inequality: the load can be at most the rating, so the answer is a range, and boxes come whole, so the end of the range is rounded down." hint: ["The load is the mower plus 40 kg for each box.", "At most 750 kg means less than or equal to."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A trailer is rated for a load of 750 kg and already carries a 90 kg mower. Each box of pavers has a mass of 40 kg. What is the most boxes that can go on?" steps: - ["Let $n$ be the number of boxes. The load is $90 + 40n$ kg", "the mower plus 40 kg for each box"] - ["$90 + 40n \\le 750$", "the load can be at most 750 kg, so 750 itself is allowed"] - ["$40n \\le 660$, so $n \\le 16.5$", "take 90 from both sides, then divide by 40: a positive number, so the sign stays"] - ["16 boxes: $90 + 16 \\times 40 = 730$ kg. 17 boxes would be 770 kg, over the limit", "boxes come whole, so go down to 16 and check both sides"] picks: - step: 4 q: "The solution is $n \\le 16.5$. How many boxes go on?" options: - "16, because half a box is not a box and 17 is over the limit" - "17, because 16.5 rounds up" - "16.5 boxes" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "17 boxes would weigh 90 + 680 = 770 kg, over 750. Round down.", "Boxes come whole. You cannot load half a box."] answer: "16" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["17", "17 boxes would weigh 770 kg. Round 16.5 down, not up."] - ["18", "That ignores the mower. The 90 kg is already on."] criteria: - "I wrote the load as 90 + 40n and used at most, not just less than." - "I checked 16 boxes and 17 boxes against 750 kg." - "My answer is a whole number of boxes." explain: "$90 + 40n \\le 750$ gives $n \\le 16.5$, so at most 16 boxes: 730 kg. A 17th box makes 770 kg." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The rating and masses are made up for the task, and on a real trailer the rating plate says whether it counts the trailer's own weight. Write the load, the inequality, solve it, then decide what to do with 16.5 and type the number of boxes. **Also used in** - **Trailers and lifts.** A rating plate is a limit: the load must be at most that, so "how many boxes" is an inequality. - **Budgets.** "How many rides can I afford after the entry fee?" has the same shape: the cost can be at most what you have. - **Next.** Two limits at once, such as a budget and a time, make a region on a graph in Year 10. ```teacher summary: Students solve one-variable inequalities like equations, reversing the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative, show solutions on a number line with open or closed circles, and check graphically and by substitution (AC9M8A02, node 3). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 13 min · Practise and Make 12 min struggle: Reversing the sign when dividing by a negative, and deciding whether the end number is in or out. Ask students to test one value from their answer in the first inequality, before they show it on the line. goals: - I can solve an inequality, reversing the inequality sign when I multiply or divide by a negative. - I can show a solution on a number line with the right circle (open or closed) and direction. - I can check a solution by substituting a value, or with a graph. before: > Do the Investigate board yourself first. Students need Solving harder equations, and Lines and regions (Linear relations) for the graph. The one idea: inequalities solve like equations, except that multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses the inequality sign, because it flips the order on the number line (2 < 5 but −2 > −5). The common mistake is keeping the inequality sign; it is planted in the Predict and in Mia's working, whose own check fails. Students show answers on the number line board (move P, choose the circle and the direction), so the board marks the solution, not the way it is written. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands, then have students test x = 0 in −2x > 6." - "Run: ask where all the working points are, and what that says about the solution." - "Investigate: model the worked example, then the number-line argument for reversing (2 < 5, −2 > −5)." - "Modify: before 5 − x > 2, ask how to get x on its own when it has a minus sign." - "Make: collect students' inequalities and check one value from each." - "Paper: the trailer task is worked in books; the page marks the number of boxes (16) and the reason for rounding down. Books out, and look for 16 and 17 both checked against 750." stuck: - see: A student keeps the sign after dividing by a negative (Mia's mistake). ask: Pick a value from your answer and check it in the first inequality. fix: If it fails, the sign should have reversed. - see: A student chooses the wrong circle. ask: Is the end number itself a solution? fix: "< and >: no, open circle. ≤ and ≥: yes, closed circle." - see: A student avoids the negative by moving x across. ask: Does that work too? fix: "Yes: −2x > 6 → 0 > 6 + 2x → −6 > 2x → −3 > x. Same answer, no reversing needed." stretch: "Solve −4 < 2x + 2 ≤ 10 (a double inequality: −3 < x ≤ 4) and show it on the line." support: Check every answer by testing one value inside and one outside the solution. leads: > This completes AC9M8A02: graphing lines and regions, solving equations, solving inequalities. Where it leads: inequalities with two variables (regions) and linear programming in later years. exit: q: Solve 7 − 2x ≥ 1 and show it on a number line. a: "−2x ≥ −6, x ≤ 3 (reversed): closed circle at 3, shaded left. Check x = 0: 7 ≥ 1." explain: > Solve an **inequality** like an equation, doing the same to both sides. Adding, subtracting, and multiplying or dividing by a **positive** keep the inequality sign. Multiplying or dividing by a **negative** reverses it: $-2x > 6$ gives $x < -3$ (because $2 < 5$ but $-2 > -5$). On a number line: an **open** circle for $<$ and $>$ (the end is not included), **closed** for $\le$ and $\ge$, shaded towards the solutions. Check by trying a value: $x = -4$ gives $8 > 6$. ✓ ```

# Boards for "Inequalities". The graph compares the two sides; the number line shows a solution as a ray.

# region: run
widget: graph
x: -6, 4
y: -4, 12
grid: 1, 2
plot: y = -2x
plot: y = 6, dashed
point P: 2, -4, drag
# endregion

# region: explain
widget: graph
x: -6, 4
y: -4, 12
grid: 1, 2
plot: y = -2x
plot: y = 6, dashed
cross: 1, 2
# endregion

# region: ray
widget: numberline
range: -10, 10
point P: 0, drag
ray: P
# endregion

# region: pic-less-5
widget: numberline
range: -2, 10
ray: x < 5
# endregion
